text:
The Capitals have lost four straight, been outscored 23-11 while doing it, and spent the week answering for things that happened away from the scoresheet. Jakob Chychrun's hit on Ottawa's Nick Cousins is still producing headlines, 30 of them in two weeks, and Tom Wilson avoided a suspension for his hit on Florida's Sandis Vilmanis. Alex Ovechkin passed everyone in franchise history for assists this month, a lovely footnote to a season CBS Sports summed up as "Struggling to contribute in 2026-27."

The odd thing is how ordinary Washington's process looks. They have 53% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of the chances), and their goal difference of -9 sits on expected goals of almost exactly even. The gap is in net and on the finish: their goalies have allowed 6.5 more goals than the shots deserved. Tonight Charlie Lindgren starts over Logan Thompson, and Lindgren is at .864 with 3.3 goals allowed above expected. That's the matchup the Capitals need to survive. Wilson hasn't scored in 16 games on 4.4 expected goals, which is the kind of drought that usually breaks. Ryan Leonard has goals in four straight.

Boston opens a six-game homestand in better shape than its last five suggests. The 4-1 win in Detroit snapped a three-game slide, and the Bruins sit at a 79% playoff chance by our numbers. Some of that is borrowed: a +19 goal difference on +3.4 expected, propped up by 10.8 goals saved above expected from their goaltending and nearly five goals of hot finishing. Jeremy Swayman is the headline, 29 of them in two weeks, at +7.0 this season. James Hagens (back) is out, and Marat Khusnutdinov has taken his spot beside Elias Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt.

Boston takes 4.8 penalties a game, a habit that gives a Washington power play room to work. Our numbers lean Boston, 3.46 expected goals to 3.04. Khusnutdinov is our sleeper at 17% to score, and David Pastrnak is at 79% for a point.
headline: Four straight losses, and a backup in net
